claims.text: What the strip looks like Complete AV dissociation: the P waves and the QRS complexes each run @ their own rate, indep of each other.
claims.quote: Complete AV dissociation Atrial and ventricular rates independent

claims.text: Aspects (abnorm in red) Rate: slow — a junctional escape runs 35–50 bpm, a ventricular escape 20–40 bpm
claims.quote: the ventricular escape rhythm is both slower (20 to 40 beats/minute) than a junctional escape rhythm (35 to 50 beats/minute)

claims.text: P waves: more P waves than QRS complexes
claims.quote: By definition, the P wave rate is greater than the QRS rate.

claims.text: PR interval: none — ⍉relationship b/n P waves and QRS complexes
claims.quote: There is no electrical communication between the atria and ventricles and thus no relationship between P waves and QRS complexes (AV dissociation).

claims.text: QRS: set by the escape rhythm — narrow (junctional escape) or wide (ventricular escape)
claims.quote: Escape rhythm determines QRS width: narrow (junctional escape) or wide (ventricular escape)

claims.text: → (mech and diagnoses) Mech: the end point of Mobitz I (AV nodal fatigue, ex, ↑vagal tone in acute inferior MI) or Mobitz II (sudden His-Purkinje failure, ex, septal infarct in anterior MI or conducting-system dz)
claims.quote: Complete heart block is essentially the end point of either Mobitz I or Mobitz II AV block It may be due to progressive fatigue of AV nodal cells as per Mobitz I (e.g. secondary to increased vagal tone in the acute phase of an inferior MI) Alternatively, it may be due to sudden onset of complete conduction failure throughout the His-Purkinje system, as per Mobitz II. This can be secondary to septal infarction in acute anterior MI, or as a result of progression of conducting system disease causing true trifascicular block

claims.text: Inferior MI, AV-nodal blocking drugs (ex, CCBs, BBs, digoxin), idiopathic degen of the conducting system (Lenègre or Lev dz)
claims.quote: Inferior myocardial infarction AV-nodal blocking drugs (e.g. calcium-channel blockers, beta-blockers, digoxin) Idiopathic degeneration of the conducting system (Lenegre’s or Lev’s disease), causing true trifascicular block

claims.text: Transient or reversible Eti incl Lyme carditis and vagally mediated block
claims.quote: Transient or reversible causes of AV block can include Lyme carditis and neurologically mediated (vagal) heart blocks.

claims.text: Up to one-third of pts aged 18–60 w new Mobitz II or third-degree block and ⍉evident struct dz have ♡ sarcoidosis
claims.quote: Up to one-third of patients age 18 years to 60 years with new-onset Mobitz II second-degree or third-degree AV block without evident structural heart disease are diagnosed with cardiac sarcoidosis after targeted investigations

claims.text: Sx Junctional (narrow) escape: faster (35–50 bpm), reliable rhythm w mild Sx — fatigue, postural light-headedness, effort intol
claims.quote: Escape rhythms originating above the bifurcation of the His bundle produce narrow QRS complexes, relatively rapid (35 to 50 beats/minute) and reliable heart rates, and mild symptoms (eg, fatigue, postural light-headedness, effort intolerance).

claims.text: Ventricular (wide) escape: slower (20–40 bpm), unreliable rhythm w severe Sx — presyncope, syncope, HF
claims.quote: Escape rhythms originating below the bifurcation produce wider QRS complexes, slower (20 to 40 beats/minute) and unreliable heart rates, and more severe symptoms (eg, presyncope, syncope, heart failure).

claims.text: Signs of AV dissociation: cannon a waves, fluctuating BP, varying loudness of S1
claims.quote: Signs include those of AV dissociation, such as cannon a waves, blood pressure fluctuations, and variation in loudness of the first heart sound (S1).

claims.text: ↑risk of ventricular standstill and sudden ♡ death
claims.quote: Patients with third degree heart block are at high risk of ventricular standstill and sudden cardiac death

claims.text: Tx Urgent admission for ♡ monitoring, backup temp pacing and USU a permanent pacemaker
claims.quote: They require urgent admission for cardiac monitoring, backup temporary pacing and usually insertion of a permanent pacemaker

claims.text: Drug-induced block: stopping the drug may work, though temp pacing may be needed
claims.quote: If the block is caused by antiarrhythmic medications, stopping the medication may be effective, although temporary pacing may be needed.

claims.text: Block from acute inferior MI (AV nodal, vagal/adenosine-mediated) may respond to atropine or aminophylline and USU resolves over several days
claims.quote: AV block caused by acute inferior myocardial infarction usually reflects atrioventricular nodal dysfunction due to increased parasympathetic tone and/or local adenosine release. It may respond to atropine or aminophylline and in most cases resolves spontaneously over several days.

claims.text: Block from anterior MI (His-Purkinje necrosis): immediate transvenous pacemaker, w external pacing in the interim
claims.quote: AV block caused by anterior myocardial infarction usually reflects extensive myocardial necrosis involving the His-Purkinje system and requires immediate transvenous pacemaker insertion with interim external pacing as necessary
